newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SUNRIGHT SAYS DROPS LEK SUN STAKE PLAN.
newsitem.headline: SUNRIGHT SAYS DROPS LEK SUN STAKE PLAN.

text.p: Sunright Ltd said on Thursday it had pulled out of a planned deal to buy a Singapore $1.3 million 30 percent stake in Malaysia's Lek Sun Manufacturing Sdn Bhd.
"We have decided not to pursue this acquisition," Sam Lim, Sunright executive chairman and chief executive, said in a statement.
Sunright said in July 1996 it had signed a memorandum of understanding with Lek Sun, but Thursday's statement said expected developments in the deal had not materialised.
But the firm, which provides burn-in testing for semiconductor chips and other electronics industry services, said it would continue the hunt for partners.
"Sunright will continue to look for opportunities to add value or complement our core business," Lim said.
